source.title: Datamine competing bounty entries: what can Tally steal?
source.body:
Datamine the other entries to zrl's AI time tracking bounty (thread under the Nov 18 post in #zrl-land, plus #ship). Goal: find ideas, code, and pitfalls Tally can steal or should avoid. Findings are posted as comments as each project is done.

## Projects with a public repo + site
- [x] **Sablier** (Alice): https://sablier.hackclub.cc · https://github.com/espcaa/sablier
- [x] **Steer** (duck/Ellie): https://steer.duck.hackclub.app · https://github.com/EwoudVV/steer
- [x] **Hindsight (repo 404, site only)** (mixid_mbb): https://hindsight.mixidthesilly.dev · https://github.com/MIXIDtheSilly/Hindsight
- [x] **StruggleTime** (derek aydin): https://62-83-116-143.sslip.io · https://github.com/derekified/struggletime

## No public code (design notes from the thread only)
- [x] **Sauron** (max gobert spork): logs every prompt, response and file edit; models reading time + prompt effort. Screenshots only.
- [x] **Lockin** (Jenin, via Amp): design doc, nothing published.
- [x] **chisel** (gorkie bot): ~1.3k lines stdlib Python, AGPLv3, only a .tar.gz Slack attachment.
- [x] **Kairos**: https://github.com/hackclub/kairos, an HQ repo, not a member submission. Worth reading as the likely "official" baseline.

## What to extract per project
- Signals captured (harness logs, editor, git, idle) and how
- How "human time" is separated from agent time
- Anti-gaming / trust approach
- Privacy posture
- Anything that contradicts or improves a Tally design decision
- Verdict: steal / adapt / avoid

Caveat: source list came from reading the thread; DMs/private channels are not covered.

comments.author: sectersion
comments.text:
## Hindsight (mixid_mbb): site only

**The repo link doesn't work.** `github.com/MIXIDtheSilly/Hindsight` returns 404 (not in the owner's public repo list), so it is private or renamed. The site says "open source AGPLv3" and points to GitHub releases, so this is based on the landing page only. I read no code.

**Model** (numbers quoted from the site):
- *Hands-on*: each prompt, edit, diff review or commit keeps the clock running **35 s**.
- *Watching*: an agent run counts if you react within **20 s** of it finishing (reply, scroll, open diff).
- *Check-in*: a mascot ("Byte") adds **5 min** per interaction and asks "what's the agent doing?" before it expires. Answering extends it.
- *Unattended*: runs while away show as hatched blocks on the timeline and are excluded from the total.
- Quick replies like "continue" earn about 1 min, not 5.

**Capture:** installer hooks Claude Code, OpenCode, VS Code, Cursor. Zed works with no setup. Git.

**Privacy claim:** only timing metadata leaves. The sample event is `prompt_submitted` with `text_len`, `typed_permille` and `content_hash`.

**Ideas for Tally**
- **`typed_permille` (steal).** The share of a prompt that was typed vs pasted is a cheap human-presence signal we don't have. A pasted 2 kB prompt and a typed one get different substance caps. Check whether it can be taken from harness logs alone. Probably not, so it likely needs a hook or an editor extension. It could be an optional feature.
- **`content_hash` (adapt).** Lets the server detect duplicate or replayed prompts without seeing text. We could add a salted hash as a numeric text feature, but check it against the privacy list in the README first. A hash of short text is brute-forceable, so use a per-user salt.
- **Hatched "unattended" timeline (steal for the dashboard).** Showing the excluded time instead of dropping it makes the subtraction visible. It matches our *unverified* bucket idea.
- **Check-in prompt (avoid).** It is a presence challenge that interrupts the user, and it is easy to script. It also contradicts "passive capture". Our OS idle timer plus action evidence is the better approach.
- **Flat per-action windows (35 s / 20 s / 5 min).** These are simpler than our claim-since-previous-action model, but they pay for activity and not for decisions. This is exactly what the bounty post complains about, so I'd keep our model.

Verdict: steal `typed_permille` and the unattended-timeline idea. Adapt the hash. Avoid the check-in.

comments.author: sectersion
comments.text:
## Sablier (Alice): the strongest entry so far

Go, AGPL-3.0 (same as ours, so porting with attribution is fine), ~25k lines, many pure-function tests. Read at `bbab5da`. I spot-checked the constants and flags below against the source. Not read: `launch.go`, `sync.go`, `launcher/relay.go`, the opencode mapper, `update.go`, the SQL.

**Capture is hook-based, not log-based.** `sablier claude|codex|opencode` wraps the harness in a PTY and injects hooks (`harness/claude/settings.go` merges into `--settings`, Codex uses `-c hooks.X=[...]`, opencode runs `opencode serve` on localhost). It never parses `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl`. Anything started outside the wrapper is invisible, and there is no Cursor, Aider, Copilot, Gemini, git or WakaTime. Tally's log-parsing approach covers more.

**Credit model** (`internal/credit/credit.go`, `Version = 3`, `AgentCap` 5 min, `InputCap` 2 min):
- Each prompt, approval or interrupt earns up to 5 min after it, plus a window before it back to the last turn end, capped at 5 min.
- Typing, mouse and scroll ticks each earn a 5 s window plus 2 min after.
- Leaving the terminal for over 2 min cuts credit from the moment you left.
- A sweep-line (`attribute()`) means overlapping time counts once. Observed input beats inferred windows.
- Flat cap per action, no substance check. One keystroke per 2 min earns continuous credit. This is the gap Tally's substance caps close.

**Input sensing (`launcher/input.go`).** Counts raw stdin in 5 s windows: key chunks, SGR/X10 mouse, bracketed paste (`\e[200~`) and focus in/out (`\e[I` / `\e[O`). Stores counts only. This is the same idea as Hindsight's `typed_permille`, done without an editor extension.

**Permission dialogs are inferred.** `PermissionRequest` followed by a matching `PostToolUse` gives approval plus its latency. A denial is synthesized from the next prompt or `Stop`. The pairing is "last PreToolUse per agent", which is fragile, but approval latency is a real human-time signal we don't use.

**Trust.**
- `event/chain.go` is sha256 over length-prefixed fields (prev, seq, ts ms, kind, session, project, harness, source, data).
- `server/ingest.go` verifies hashes and seq/prev, treats an identical re-send as a duplicate and a different one as a 409, and rejects timestamps over 5 min ahead.
- `server/flags.go` marks events late, stale (over 24 h), backfill (days) or unchained, and a reviewer sees them.
- The chain is unkeyed, so a forged chain from seq 1 verifies. It only detects edits after upload. Ours has the same limit unless the server witness closes it, which is worth stating in our threat model.
- `sablier verify` has the server sample prompts, the client uploads the text, and an LLM labels each as iteration or delegation. There is an HMAC of the prompt so uploaded text matches what was sent. This is opt-in, but the text goes to a third-party model.

**Privacy.** Metadata, project id (git remote or folder name), install UUID and prompt HMACs leave. Prompt text stays in local sqlite. `install.sh` verifies a sha256 from the same origin as the binary, so it protects against corruption and not tampering, and `SABLIER_RELEASE_URL` can redirect the download.

## Verdicts
| Item | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Bracketed-paste / focus-escape input counting | **steal** (optional wrapper mode) |
| Approval latency as human time | **steal** |
| Pure `Map(state, hook) -> (state, events)` adapters, tested without I/O | **steal** (test style) |
| "Don't guess when the lower bound is unknown" | **steal** |
| `Version` constant on the scoring rules | already have (ruleset), keep |
| Late / stale / backfill flags on the server | **steal** |
| Sweep-line overlap resolution | **adapt**, check against our claim-since-previous-action |
| Hook wrapper as a capture source | **adapt**, optional next to log parsing. Hook-injected `--settings` can clash with user settings |
| Flat 5 min after-window | **avoid** (pays for reading time) |
| Unended turn treated as busy forever | **avoid** |
| LLM verify with prompt upload | **avoid** (breaks "no text leaves"). Our self-hosted judge is better |
| `install.sh` | **adapt**, add signature verification |

comments.author: sectersion
comments.text:
## Steer (duck/Ellie): closest to Tally's design, v0.5.9

Rust client ~5.5k lines, Node server ~2.2k lines, AGPL-3.0-or-later (compatible with ours). Action-claim model like ours. Spot-checked `AGENT_TIMEOUT = 600` (`analyze.rs:11`), `gap_credit` (`analyze.rs:317`) and `AGENT_QUIET = 60` (`evidence.rs:32`). Not read: `live.rs` (1374 lines), `watch.rs`, `editor.rs`, `checkin.rs`, most of `server.mjs`, the browser extension, and the live site.

**Capture**
- Claude Code: hooks plus `~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl`, skipping `isSidechain`. Fields it reads: `isMeta`, `isCompactSummary`, `origin.kind`, `turnOrigin`, `promptSource`, `toolDenialKind == "user-rejected"`.
- Codex: `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl` (`session_meta`, `turn_context.approval_policy`, `event_msg task_complete/turn_aborted`, `content_item_kinds`).
- Copilot (`~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl`) and OpenCode (`opencode.db`, read-only) are marked in the source as written from docs and not tried against real use.
- Also a VS Code/Cursor extension and a Chrome extension for chatgpt.com and claude.ai. No Aider or Gemini CLI.

**Human vs agent time**
- The gap from the agent's last step to the next prompt goes through `gap_credit`. The first 60 s count in full (300 s if the human acted first or tested), then an exponential fade (240 s time constant), a ~300 s max, and a break above 1800 s credits only 120 s.
- Typing = chars/4 s clamped to 5-300 s, pasted text excluded.
- Every prompt is capped by wall-clock since the previous human action. First prompt in a session is capped at 120 s. Generic prompts are capped at 120 s.
- **Dark-flow rule:** three or more generic or near-repeat prompts within 900 s with no test keep only 30 s each.
- Interrupts, shell commands, slash commands and rejections have their own clamps (5-300 s, 10-300 s, 5-30 s, 10-60 s).
- Their idle events exist but the README says they don't count toward anything yet.

**Trust**
- Server stamps arrival time, drops events more than 300 s off, token buckets, 20k events per account per day, 12 h/day and 60 h/week caps.
- Heuristic flags (replies ~8 s after a stop, very even intervals, long days with no break), commits checked against the GitHub API within 15 min, human reviewers can approve, cut or reject.
- **`web/trust.html` admits a rhythm-faking script earned 4-6 h/day undetected.** No hash chain, no client signing.

**Privacy.** Counts only (words, chars, images, specific/observation/generic/repeat), project name, session id, timestamps. The README lists every field. Risks: self-update downloads a release binary with only a size and `steer version` check, `curl | sh` install, edits `~/.cursor/hooks.json` and Claude settings, pages public by default, reviewer API exposes per-user events. **Good:** `evidence.rs` avoids `git status` / `git log` in untrusted repos (fsmonitor and filters can run code) and uses `ls-files`, `rev-parse`, `cat-file` with timeouts.

## Verdicts
| Item | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `claude.rs` `user_event` filters (`isMeta`, `isCompactSummary`, `origin.kind`, injected prefixes) | **steal**. Check ours against it for missed injected-prompt kinds |
| `toolDenialKind == "user-rejected"` as a decision signal | **steal**. Fits "hours of decisions" |
| Codex `content_item_kinds` (typed vs injected AGENTS.md) | **steal** |
| Pasted text excluded from typing time | **steal** |
| Safe git evidence (no `git status`/`log` in untrusted repos) | **steal**. Audit our git adapter |
| Overlap-once interval merge, git "agent quiet for 60 s" rule | **steal** |
| `gap_credit` exponential fade, no cliff | **adapt**. Constants were fitted to their own sim, refit on ours |
| Dark-flow loop rule | **adapt** into our substance caps |
| Server skew correction (events more than 300 s off) | **adapt** (we have witnessed pushes, add skew) |
| Rhythm-faking red-team | **do it ourselves**. Plan 12's red-team already found the scorer caps per action, not per hour. Run their script idea against us |
| English word lists for observation/generic classification | **avoid** (gameable, English-only, duplicated in JS and Rust with a parity test) |
| Unsigned self-update, public-by-default pages, adapters listed as supported but untested | **avoid** |

comments.author: sectersion
comments.text:
## StruggleTime (derek aydin): weak, mostly dead code

Rust workspace + Python `server.py` (~2.4k lines), ~23.7k lines total, AGPL-3.0, one commit. **Not an LLM judge and not a log parser.** Read: all of `st-core` and `st-daemon`, most of `st-helper/adapters.rs`, the Claude Code and shell hooks, batch-ingest (`server.py` ~2085-2235), calibration and privacy docs. Not read: `st-tray`, `st-server`, `src/verify.py`, docs-site, the Godot/Unity/JetBrains/neovim adapters, CI.

**Capture.** `st-daemon/src/lib.rs` polls the project tree every 1 s (mtime and size per file), and drains `~/.aitime/agent_events.jsonl` and `exec.jsonl`. The Claude Code hook just `printf`s a fixed JSON line on PostToolUse/Stop. It never reads `~/.claude/projects`. No Cursor/Aider/Copilot/Gemini logs, no OS idle, no git (`commits` is hardcoded 0).

**"Struggle".**
- Agent vs human is a file-change burst heuristic: 5+ files in a second, or 3+ files over 8,000 bytes, counts as AI. A formatter or `git checkout` looks like an agent. Agent time is never subtracted.
- `verify.rs::weight()` is a first-match state machine (`AI_STRUGGLE`/`STRUGGLE_LOOP`/`CLOSED_LOOP` 1.0, `AI_REVIEWED` 0.85, `HUMAN_UNVERIFIED` 0.70, `EXEC_ONLY` 0.50, `AI_UNREVIEWED` 0.25, `OPEN_LOOP_AGENT_DUMP` 0.20).
- `is_ai_struggle()` depends on counters (`same_file_reedit_count`, `ai_retry_loops`, `test_fail_to_pass_transitions`, `agent_turn_churn`) that the Rust daemon doesn't produce, so most of it is dead code. What actually gives full weight is `exec_failures>0 && executions>1 && (human_edit||commit)`: a failed command, another command, then any file change.
- The "20/20 calibration" is author-labelled synthetic fixtures run against the same rules. Circular.

**Trust is weak.**
- Unkeyed SHA-256 chain, and `ensure_sync_shape` rewrites and re-hashes old entries.
- Per-install Ed25519 signing exists only in Python. The Rust daemon sends `install_id: "rust-daemon"` unsigned, and the server accepts and weights unsigned buckets.
- The server trusts client-sent `active_secs`.
- Anyone can append to `agent_events.jsonl`. Dedup is on identical lines, so a changing field defeats it.

**Privacy.** Good: `FORBIDDEN_KEYS` (`st-core/src/agent_events.rs:8`) is rejected recursively in daemon and server, and file ids are `sha256(salt:path)[..16]`. Sloppy: `fetch_adapters_from_github` downloads and installs the adapters from an unpinned `refs/heads/main`, the shell hook logs the git subcommand, docs hardcode a domain that isn't the live host, evidence is retained after account deletion.

**License:** AGPL-3.0, same as ours, so code reuse is legal with attribution. Nothing here is worth porting anyway.

## Verdicts
| Item | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Shared `FORBIDDEN_KEYS` check at the daemon *and* server boundary, recursive | **steal**. Check we reject unknown fields on the server, not only omit them in the daemon |
| Cap activity ticks per drain so a retry storm can't inflate time | **steal** (verify our per-action cap covers it) |
| Fail, another run, then an edit as a cheap struggle signal | **adapt**, only from real harness events, never from file mtime |
| Silent-streak decay across buckets | **avoid**. Per-bucket decay makes weights depend on bucket alignment |
| File-burst size as the agent/human split | **avoid** |
| Heartbeats counted as human edits | **avoid** |
| Unkeyed chain, unsigned buckets accepted, trusting client `active_secs` | **avoid** |
| Self-labelled synthetic calibration | **avoid**. Calibrate on real labelled sessions |

comments.author: sectersion
comments.text:
## Kairos (hackclub/kairos): HQ's own tracker, a direct competitor

Not a member submission. Rust workspace (core, agent, cli, server on Axum + Postgres, sim, release), ~55k lines, one squashed commit (v0.1.18), AGPL-3.0, so we can port code with attribution. The README says it "tracks your focus time while you build with AI". The landing page splits a session into focus time and excluded "agent time" (example: 35 min session, 16m40s focus, 18 min agent removed). Spot-checked `credit.rs` constants (`THINK_SECS`, `ANSWER_THINK_SECS`, `REVISION = 7`). Not read: `web/review.rs` (1,459 lines), `api/events.rs` and ingest validation, auth and trust-level logic, the agent recorder, `crates/sim`, the extension. **I did not find payout or approval logic, so whether this is "the official method" is unverified.**

**Capture.** ~13 harness readers in `crates/core/src/sources/*.rs`: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini, Cline, opencode, Qwen, Pi, Hermes and others. The `kairosd` daemon (`crates/agent`) writes a hash-chained event log (`core/src/event.rs`: `seal`/`digest`) with Prompt (word count, `pasted` flag), AgentStart, ReplyDone (words, tool count, files changed), Answered, Focus (window class), Present (per-second input bitmask sent once a minute), Idle, FileSave, Commit, Heartbeat.

**WakaTime interception.** It intercepts wakatime-cli heartbeats locally and forwards them to the previous endpoint, usually Hackatime (`agent/src/wakatime.rs`). It takes over the WakaTime config and the API port. **Tally must not also rewrite `~/.wakatime.cfg`: two daemons doing this will fight** (`keep`/`park` logic).

**Credit** (`core/src/credit.rs`, `credit_v8`, causal, server-side per user, old v1-v7 kept so stored credit can be rebuilt on a `REVISION` bump):
- `READ_WPM` 230, `TYPE_WPM` 35, pasted prompts count at most 60 typed words, prompts under 3 words get nothing.
- `THINK_SECS` 120, `LOOKBACK_SECS` 600. Answering an agent question: 30 s think time, capped 600 s. Replies can be read for 7200 s after finishing.
- Gaps of 180 s or less are bridged if the person was active for 5 s on both sides. While an agent runs, only 30 s after the person's last input counts.
- Editor time during an agent turn counts only within 120 s of a human write heartbeat. Heartbeats more than 600 s late are ignored.
- It is time-window based (reading, typing and answering earn bounded time), not per-action claims with substance caps like ours.

**Trust and privacy.** Same privacy contract as ours: times, counts, project names and file lists only, no code, prompts, replies, titles or URLs, no screenshots. Controls: `kairos exclude`, `pause`, `uninstall`. The chain is not witnessed by the server as far as I read. `server/src/signals.rs` has advisory signals that never change credit (days over 12 h, 4 h unbroken input, overlapping devices, uploads over 48 h late, 5 h with no output, timestamps too far off). Real trust is a human reviewer (`web/review.rs`) plus a per-user `trust_level`.

**Integration.** The read API mirrors Hackatime's (`/api/v1/users/{u}/stats`, `projects`, `heartbeats/spans`, `trust_factor`, leaderboards), with `kp_` program keys (`server/src/programs.rs`). I found no documented third-party submission path.

## Verdicts
| Item | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Session-log readers in `core/src/sources/*` for harnesses we both cover | **steal** (AGPL both ways). Biggest win in this whole issue. Diff against our adapters for formats we're missing |
| Human write heartbeat required for editor credit during an agent turn | **adapt** |
| `human_lines` / `ai_lines` heartbeat fields to filter agent-written lines | **adapt** |
| Late-heartbeat cutoff (600 s) | **adapt** |
| Advisory-only signals that never change credit | **adapt**. Keeps reviewers informed without rule creep |
| Versioned credit rules, old versions kept, rebuild on bump | **already have** (ruleset ids and one ledger chain per ruleset). Compare what happens to an already-published ledger |
| `crates/sim` persona-based simulator | **steal** the idea. Good fit for plan 12's red-team |
| Read API shaped like Hackatime's | **consider** a compatible read endpoint so existing consumers can swap the base URL |
| Time-window credit model | **avoid**. Our per-action claim plus substance caps is stricter against idling and automation |
| Rewriting WakaTime config / taking the API port | **avoid**, and make sure we coexist |
| Trusting client timestamps without a witness | **avoid**. Our server-witnessed pushes are a real differentiator |

**Positioning.** If Kairos is the HQ baseline, Tally's pitch is witnessed hashes and a per-action substance cap, not another time tracker. Worth checking in #hq whether it is the official method before more time goes into overlap.

comments.author: sectersion
comments.text:
## No public code: Sauron, Lockin, chisel

Nothing to read. All I have is the one-line description from the thread, so there is nothing to steal yet.
- **Sauron** (max gobert spork): logs every prompt, response and file edit and models reading time plus prompt effort. Screenshots only. Logging responses and edits is the opposite of our privacy rule. The "prompt effort" model is the same idea as our substance caps. Re-check if code appears.
- **Lockin** (Jenin, via Amp): design doc, nothing published.
- **chisel** (gorkie bot): ~1.3k lines of stdlib Python, AGPLv3, only a .tar.gz Slack attachment, no repo or site. Fetching it from Slack would be the only way to read it, and I can't from here. If someone can download it, it's small enough to read in one sitting.

## Summary: what to do, ranked

Every readable repo is AGPL-3.0 like ours, so porting with attribution is legal. None of them has our combination of per-action substance caps and a server-witnessed ledger. Kairos (HQ) is the one that decides positioning.

1. **Diff our harness parsers against Kairos `core/src/sources/*` and Steer `claude.rs` / `codex.rs`.** Cheapest, highest value. Steer's injected-prompt filters (`isMeta`, `isCompactSummary`, `origin.kind`, `toolDenialKind`, Codex `content_item_kinds`) are small and concrete.
2. **Audit our git adapter against Steer's `evidence.rs`.** It avoids `git status` / `git log` on untrusted repos because fsmonitor and filters can run code. If ours calls either, that's a security fix, not a nicety.
3. **Treat user rejections and permission-approval latency as decision signals** (Steer `toolDenialKind`, Sablier approval latency). It fits "hours of decisions" directly.
4. **Typed vs pasted** (Hindsight `typed_permille`, Kairos `pasted` flag, Steer excludes pasted text, Sablier counts bracketed paste). Four projects converge on it, so we should too. Check whether the logs give us this.
5. **Server-side handling:** late/stale/backfill flags (Sablier), advisory-only signals that never change credit (Kairos), clock-skew correction (Steer), and rejecting forbidden keys on the server as well as the daemon (StruggleTime).
6. **Red-team with their attacks.** Steer's own page admits a rhythm-faking script earns 4-6 h/day. Kairos has a persona simulator (`crates/sim`). Plan 12's red-team already found the scorer caps per action and not per hour, so this is the same finding.
7. **Optional hook/PTY wrapper capture** (Sablier) for high-fidelity input counting. Not before 1-6.
8. **Dashboard:** Hindsight's hatched "unattended" blocks make the subtracted time visible, which fits our unverified bucket.

**Not worth taking:** flat per-action windows (Sablier 5 min, Hindsight 35 s/5 min), file-burst agent detection and unkeyed chains (StruggleTime), English word-list classifiers (Steer), check-in prompts (Hindsight), prompt-text upload to a third-party model (Sablier `verify`), unsigned self-update (Steer).

**Open questions**
- Is Kairos the official method? Someone in #hq was asking. If yes, decide whether Tally emits to it, coexists with it, or competes. Either way, don't rewrite `~/.wakatime.cfg`.
- Hindsight's repo returned 404, so confirm whether it's private before it is cited as open source.
- Findings come from reading code by sub-agents with spot checks on constants and licenses. Anything marked "not read" in a comment is unreviewed.

comments.author: sectersion
comments.text:
## Implementation writeups for every "steal"

I read Tally's code for each item and measured the log-related ones against my own `~/.claude/projects` (structure-only scripts that print counts and lengths, never text, in `datamine/scripts/`). **That changed several verdicts:** two items are real bugs in our parser, two were already built, and one (git hardening) needs no change. Ordered by value. "Ruleset" means whether `RULESET_VERSION` ("2026.11-0", `ruleset.rs:3`) would need a bump, which starts a new ledger chain.

---

### 1. Compaction summaries are scored as human prompts (bug, from Steer's filters)
**Evidence.** Of 650 human-classified prompts in my logs, **3 have `isCompactSummary: true`** (also `isVisibleInTranscriptOnly`) and start with "This session is being continued from a previous conversation". `line.rs:94-98` treats `origin.kind == "human"` as the whole test, so each becomes a `HumanPrompt` with a huge `chars` and, because the summary quotes project vocabulary, a high `relevance_pm`. That earns the top prompt cap (`caps.rs:40`, up to 1200 s) for text nobody typed.
**Change.** In `claude_code/line.rs::user`, before the `human` check, return `vec![]` if any of `isMeta`, `isCompactSummary`, `isVisibleInTranscriptOnly`, `isVirtual` is true. Add Steer's prefix list as a second guard on the text (`claude.rs:183`: `<task-notification>`, `<local-command-stdout>`, `<local-command-stderr>`, `<bash-stdout>`, `<bash-stderr>`, `Caveat:`, "This session is being continued…"), because the `origin`-absent fallback path (3 of 368 in FORMAT.md) has no other protection.
**Test.** Two fixture lines in `tests/fixtures/claude_code` (compact summary with `origin.kind: human`, and an `origin`-less line with an injected prefix), plus cases in `line.rs` tests next to `human_prompt_vs_task_notification_vs_sidechain`. Record the flags in `FORMAT.md` deviations.
**Ruleset.** No (parser only). Already-finalized history isn't rescanned (`finalized_through`), so past summaries stay counted unless `repair.rs` re-reads. Decide whether to backfill.
**Size.** ~15 lines + fixtures.

### 2. Human tool rejections are dropped (bug, from Steer's `toolDenialKind`)
**Evidence.** My logs have **27 `user` entries with `toolDenialKind: "user-rejected"` and no `permissionDecision`**. `line.rs:118-128` emits a `ToolDecision` only when `permissionDecision.source` exists and isn't `config`, so all 27 human denials produce a `ToolResult` and nothing else. (The other kinds seen are `automode-unavailable` ×4, `permission-rule` ×1, `interrupted` ×1. Those are automatic or already an `Interrupt`, so ignore them.) A rejection is the clearest "human decision" there is and carries `DENY_CAP_MS` = 180 s (`caps.rs:14`).
**Change.** In the same function, if no `permissionDecision` is present and `v["toolDenialKind"] == "user-rejected"` with a `tool_result` in the content, push `ToolDecision { decision: Deny, n: 0 }`. The id stays `tool_decision:0`, so a later parser that sees both forms dedups.
**Test.** Fixture line plus a `line.rs` case. Update `FORMAT.md` answer 1 (it says rejects are all `source: config`, which was true of the dirs measured then).
**Ruleset.** No. Same backfill caveat as item 1.
**Size.** ~8 lines.

### 3. Typed vs pasted (Hindsight `typed_permille`, Kairos `pasted`, Steer `typed_part`)
**Evidence.** 24 of my human prompts contain `<pasted_content id="…">…</pasted_content id="…">` blocks. **Pastes are 99% of those prompts' characters**; median total 1,569 chars vs median **20 typed**; **11 of the 24 have under 20 typed chars**. Today `features.rs:84` counts `chars` over the whole text and `prompt_features` computes relevance over it too, so a pasted file full of project identifiers inflates `relevance_pm`. `novelty_bytes` against the context tail only catches pastes of what's already in context.
Format note: Kairos's `unwrap_pastes` (`core/src/parse.rs:294`) handles the 2.1.x closing tag with the id. **Steer's `typed_part` expects `</pasted_content>` without an id and misses it**, so don't copy that one. My logs also contain a bare `</pasted_content>` and `<pasted_content ...>` variants, so match the tag family and cap id length like Kairos does.
**Change, two steps so we measure before we change hours.**
- A. In `features.rs::prompt_numbers` (and a small `split_pastes(text) -> (typed, pasted_chars)` helper next to it), emit a new numeric feature `pasted_pm` = pasted chars × 1000 / total chars. Don't change scoring. Add the key to `kind_features` (`score.rs:165`) and the README privacy list, because it's a new numeric text feature.
- B. After a few weeks of data, decide whether relevance should be computed on typed text only, with pasted text counting toward `novelty_bytes` but not `relevance_pm`. Pasting a fresh stack trace with "fix this" is legitimate and is the workflow Tally is built around, so don't zero it. That's a calibration call with labelled sessions.
**Test.** Unit tests for the splitter on all tag variants above and on an unclosed tag (must not panic or drop text).
**Ruleset.** Step A adds a feature key to hashed ledger entries, so yes, bump. Step B also.
**Size.** A ≈ 40 lines. B ≈ 10 lines plus calibration.

### 4. Features and reasons are unvalidated on the server (StruggleTime `FORBIDDEN_KEYS`)
**Evidence.** `LedgerEntry` (`ledger.rs:12`) has `kind: String`, `reasons: Vec<String>`, `features: BTreeMap<String, i64>`. `verify_chain` (`ledger.rs:96`) checks only `prev_hash` and `hash`, and `checkBatch` (`server/src/ledger.ts:55`) adds ruleset and project. A modified client can upload any feature key or reason string, and the server stores and publishes them to `tally-data`. **Change.** Add `validate_entry(e: &LedgerEntry) -> Result<(), &'static str>` in `tally-scoring/src/ledger.rs`: `kind` must be one of the strings from `kind_features`, every reason must be in the list at `score.rs:140-147`, and every feature key must be in that kind's allowed list. Call it from `verify_chain` (so the same Rust runs in the daemon and, via WASM, in the server) with a new `bad_shape` reason. Keep it ruleset-scoped: the allowlist lives next to `RULESET_VERSION` so a new ruleset can add keys.
**Test.** Entry with feature `"hello_world": 1` fails `bad_shape`; every claim `score()` produces passes (reuse `synthetic(4000)`).
**Ruleset.** No for 2026.11-0 *if* the allowlist matches what's emitted today. Add item 3's `pasted_pm` in the same change as its bump.
**Size.** ~40 lines.

### 6. Agent-quiet rule for commit attribution (Steer `AGENT_QUIET`, `evidence.rs:32,182`)
**Evidence.** `git.rs:39` marks a commit as the agent's only if `has_agent_commit_marker` finds a Claude Code Bash-commit marker within −120 s/+5 s (`store.rs:650`). The Copilot adapter emits `AgentBusy` (`adapters/copilot.rs`) but no markers, so a Copilot-made commit becomes `Actor::User`, `is_human_action()` is true, and it claims up to `COMMIT_CAP_MS` = 600 s. The same will happen for each adapter we add.
**Change.** In `StoreLookup::is_agent_commit`, also return true if any `agent_busy` event from any source in the same project group covers `[commit_ts - 60 s, commit_ts]`. That needs one store query next to `has_agent_commit_marker`. The failure direction is safe: a user commit made while an agent runs in the same project is under-credited, not over-credited.
**Test.** Next to the existing `agent_commit_marker_matches_by_agent_project_and_window_only` (`store.rs:668`), plus a `git.rs` test with a fake `AgentCommitLookup`.
**Ruleset.** No (it's attribution in the daemon, but it changes emitted `Commit.by`; note it in the plan). **Size.** ~25 lines.

### 11. Optional wrapper: typed/paste/focus counts (Sablier `launcher/input.go`)
Largest item, and the only one that adds a new capture mode. Also notable: `presence::supported()` is `cfg!(windows)` (`presence.rs:37`), so today **macOS and Linux have no presence signal at all**. A `tally run -- claude` PTY wrapper that counts key chunks, bracketed-paste (`\e[200~`) and focus events (`\e[I` / `\e[O`) in 5 s windows and emits `Idle` spans would cover both gaps at once, but it only sees sessions started through it. For non-Windows presence alone, a platform `idle_ms()` is smaller and fits the existing `Platform` trait (`presence.rs:15`). Counts only, no content, as in Sablier.
